newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to Mar 21.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to Mar 21.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 58.3 percent rise in its turnover in the week ending March 21 due to renewed trade in the central bank short-term bonds.
Total turnover rose to 42.58 million dinars ($7.62 million) in 215 transactions from 26.897 million dinars in 189 deals a week ago.

"The BSE turnover rose on renewed trade in the central bank short-term bonds. Otherwise, the bourse activity is dominated by commercial paper market segment fetching an almost 80 percent of the total turnover," BSE spokesman Milko Stimac told Reuters.

"Companies have been active borrowers on the market since the beginning of 1997 but the size of their borrowing, raised from other companies, indicates there are sufficient funds within the enterprise sector," Stimac said.
Traders said demand for the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) short-term bonds rose after the central bank issued additional explanation of its 15 percent reserve requirement regulation.

The NBY said the rule, obliging banks to set aside 15 percent of their deposits but also to deposit with the NBY 15 percent of money lent to other banks, did not refer to activity between commercial banks and the central bank.
For the week ending March 21, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 196 times for a volume of 27.203 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for 0.835 million dinars in eight deals.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent, while maturity stood between seven and 30 days.
* There were two deals in the central bank short-term bonds totalling 13 million dinars.
* The bourse reported four deals in wheat contracts worth 0.833 million dinars.
*Certificates of deposit traded five times for a total of 0.709 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper, treasury bills and certificates of deposit rose to 24.188 million dinars from 22.789 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading surplus liquidity, rose to 13.978 million dinars from 13.55 million a week ago. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
